title: Subjects
why: Grouping samples by subject — patient, animal, culture, slide — keeps two samples from the same person out of different training splits, where the metric would measure memory instead of generalization.
patternHelp: Use {{marca}} where the identifier is and * for the rest. Example: {{ejemplo}} extracts P0031 from P0031_ax_012.jpg
unmatchedStay: Files that do not match stay unassigned: they never get a guessed subject.
csvHelp: Two-column file: filename and subject, separated by comma, semicolon or tab.
mapUnused: {{count}} rows in the file match no image in this project.
privacy: The subject is exported and travels with the project. If you load a real clinical identifier, pseudonymising it is your responsibility.
subject: Subject
modelBreakdown: Of what a model suggested ({{pct}}% of the corpus): {{accepted}} accepted unchanged and {{corrected}} corrected.
unknownNote: {{count}} labels predate provenance tracking: it cannot be said whether they were drawn by hand or accepted from a model.
rejectedNote: {{count}} model suggestions were rejected ({{pct}}% of everything the model proposed). They are not part of the corpus, but without them the hit rate would be computed only over what survived.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.what: Records every change that affects the labels — what changed, who and when — hash-chained, inside the project folder. It does not store geometries or masks.
audit.truncated: The last line was left half-written by an abrupt shutdown. It does not invalidate anything before it: it is discarded when the log is reopened.
audit.empty: No log yet: the project has not changed since auditing exists.
